content:
maya: Heads up — new model bring-up (redwood/model-v2.1) with FP8 + AWQ quant pipeline shows a weird accuracy skew on sql2text. Hallucination spike for numeric table cells, formatting mangled. :eyes:
raj: Numbers? how big a spike?
maya: Quick summary from yesterday's canary: baseline fp32 exact-match 92.1%, AWQ-INT8 90.6% (ok), FP8 88.9% (regression). But for a subset of queries (joins + numeric aggregations) FP8 returns wrong column values or inserts repeated zeros.
olga: Is it length / batch dependent? any correlation with batch size or KV-cache?
maya: Repro is stronger with batching > 8. At batch=1 FP8 is ~90.8, batch=32 drops to 85.3 on that subset. AWQ-int8 also degrades slightly with big batches but not as badly.
ci-bot: [automation] nightly-eval/redwood/model-v2.1/fp8 -> failed sql2text threshold (delta -3.2) — run id: 2026-03-18_23:10
dave: Can you paste the eval command you used?
maya: Sure:
```
./run_eval.sh --model redwood/model-v2.1 --quant fp8 --profile throughput --batch 32 --dataset sql2text --seed 123
```
sophie: Any kernel/runtime differences between throughput profile vs low-latency? e.g., fused attention or different GEMM path?
maya: Yes — throughput profile enables continuous batching and kernel fusion. When I switch to profile=low-latency (batch=1) the issue mostly goes away. So looks like a batching/kernel interaction with FP8 path.
raj: Could be accumulation precision or placement of requantization op. Also check KV-eviction or cache indexing differences across batched requests.
olmga: (typo) sorry, olga: Also try forcing deterministic seeds to rule out per-request RNG differences: set env RDW_QUANT_SEED and RDW_RUNTIME_SEED.
dave: I ran a quick bisect: FP8 without kernel fusion -> no regression; FP8 + fusion -> regression -> points at fused GEMM quant path.
infra-bot: deploy:canary -> redwood/model-v2.1 fp8 fusion=false on pool-ml-3 completed (3 instances)
maya: Confirmed: canary with fusion=false restored sql2text exact-match to 91.7 (close to AWQ). So fusion + FP8 seems to trigger numerical instability for batched KV shapes.
sophie: Two mitigations: 1) disable fusion on FP8 until we fix kernels, 2) add routing rule: for routes with structured-output/sql2text -> prefer AWQ-int8 or fp32. We can implement quick per-route fallback in console.
raj: Also need a repro minimal test (small harness) that reproduces the failure deterministically. If we can craft a synthetic batch that triggers the issue we can root cause faster.
maya: I'll add a minimal test set (10 queries) and push to the eval repo. Patch name: sql2text-fp8-fusion-repro.
ci-bot: [ci] Created PR #4123: add sql2text-fp8-fusion-repro (maya)
dave: For triage: ask kernel team to dump intermediate activations around the fused GEMM in FP8 code path. Tagging @eng-runtime.
olmga: olga: Also check quant scale calibration code — maybe the per-batch scale update is non-threadsafe under fusion.
sophie: If we need a short-term product fix: route sql2text -> model-v2.1@awq-int8 in prod for 24h, monitor alerts. I'll open a routing change request.
maya: I can rollback the fp8 canary and apply the AWQ route. Will also add an eval gate to prevent fp8+fusion from being rolled into dedicated pools.
raj: Good. Also add bench: latency/TP for fusion=false vs true to quantify cost of disabling fusion.
maya: Quick numbers: throughput profile (fusion=true) avg latency 95ms p50, fusion=false 120ms p50; cost - roughly +12% tokens/sec delta.
dave: Ok tradeoff. Action items: maya -> repro + PR, olga -> check quant calib thread-safety, eng-runtime -> investigate fused GEMM FP8 numerics, sophie -> routing + temporary fallback.
maya: I'll file an internal bug and link PR/CI. Thanks all :thumbsup:
raj: adding note — if we find it's batch-shape dependent we might implement shape-aware routing (small-batch FP8, large-batch AWQ) to keep perf.
maya: Opening bug: BUG-2026-1194 "FP8 fused-GEMM numerical instability with batching -> sql2text hallucinations" and linking logs + dump.
infra-bot: incident-tracker: BUG-2026-1194 created, priority P2
sophie: I'll monitor metrics overnight and report if we see production upticks.
maya: Will update thread when repro PR lands.
raj: Thanks, everyone.
